bounded_conjecture.statement: Two typed trivalent junctions joined through distinguished principal arms undergo, under non-pair-selective global drive, a deterministic local 2→2 four-boundary topological rewrite whose output depends only on junction states and boundary.
non_claims: The cited work does not establish interaction-net rewriting.
The cited work does not establish a unique pair-indexed local rule or local rule selection.
No proposed public-only coordinate is canonical or admitted.

sources.citation: Wu, Valenzuela, Bowick, and Smalyukh, Topological Rigidity and Non-Abelian defect junctions in chiral nematic systems with effective biaxial symmetry, arXiv:2410.19293.
sources.supported_claim: The work reports Q8-classified non-Abelian defect algebra, topologically rigid bound pairs, and trivalent junctions as building blocks of multi-junction trivalent networks in laboratory chiral nematics, with analysis and modeling.
sources.excluded_inference: It does not establish interaction-net rewriting.

sources.citation: Hall, Tai, Kauffman, and Smalyukh, Fusion and fission of particle-like chiral nematic vortex knots, Nature Physics 22, 103–111 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41567-025-03107-0.
sources.supported_claim: The work reports fusion, fission, and reconnection of chiral-nematic vortex knots under electric pulses, conservation of the reported topological invariant, graph-like intermediate structures, and laser-tweezer guidance of some reconnections.
sources.excluded_inference: It does not establish a unique pair-indexed interaction-net rule or local rule selection.

items.title: Define a minimal conservative formal fragment for the proposed junction rewrite
items.open_problem: Can the proposed two-junction 2→2 rewrite be stated as a finite typed local rule with an explicit conserved boundary and no hidden global selector?
items.why_open: The cited defect algebra and observed reconnections do not supply an interaction-net signature, typing discipline, or reduction semantics.
items.scope: A formal candidate language for typed trivalent junction states, distinguished arms, four-boundary interfaces, and one bounded rewrite family.
items.next_discriminating_criticism_or_test: Attempt to construct two indistinguishable local inputs whose allowed outputs differ only because of global context; such a pair criticizes locality of the formal fragment.
items.non_claims: This topic does not claim that the formal rule exists in chiral nematics, is universal, confluent, computationally complete, or physically implementable.

items.title: Simulate conditional locality and diamond tests for overlapping rewrites
items.open_problem: Do independently enabled local junction rewrites commute, or does their outcome depend on update order, remote state, or the applied pulse history?
items.why_open: Neither cited source tests interaction-net confluence, conditional locality, or critical-pair behavior.
items.scope: Finite defect-graph simulations over explicitly declared local states, boundaries, drive schedules, and overlapping redexes.
items.next_discriminating_criticism_or_test: Enumerate bounded overlapping rewrite pairs and run a diamond test; record any pair whose terminal boundary state depends on reduction order.
items.non_claims: Passing a finite simulation suite would not establish physical realization, general confluence, or computation beyond the simulated fragment.

items.title: Test whether Q8 junction pairs support a repeatable local 2→2 material mechanism
items.open_problem: Can selected Q8-classified trivalent junction pairs be prepared and driven so that the same typed local input and boundary repeatedly yield one 2→2 output?
items.why_open: The cited laboratory work establishes rich defect structure and driven reconnections, not the conjectured deterministic pair-local mechanism.
items.scope: Chiral-nematic samples, typed junction preparation, declared boundary conditions, non-pair-selective global electric drive, and repeat trials.
items.next_discriminating_criticism_or_test: Blindly repeat matched preparations while varying remote graph context; failure of output invariance criticizes the proposed local mechanism.
items.non_claims: This topic does not claim LiTaO3 relevance, a validated device, interaction-net computation, or detector calibration.

items.title: Validate optical reconstruction of typed defect-graph rewrites
items.open_problem: Can optical observations distinguish junction type, principal-arm connectivity, boundary state, and 2→2 outcomes without analysis-induced topology changes?
items.why_open: Graph-like structures in imagery do not by themselves validate a typed defect-graph readout or exclude ambiguous projections.
items.scope: Matched optical modalities, reconstruction algorithms, synthetic controls, blinded labels, and topology-preserving uncertainty reports.
items.next_discriminating_criticism_or_test: Compare independent modalities and human-blinded reconstructions on the same event; systematic disagreement criticizes the observation interface.
items.non_claims: This topic does not treat an image resemblance as evidence of interaction-net semantics or a correct local rewrite.

items.title: Separate global triggering from hidden external rule selection
items.open_problem: Does a non-pair-selective global pulse merely enable local state-dependent dynamics, or do spatial fields and guided intervention select which reconnection occurs?
items.why_open: Electric pulses and laser-tweezer guidance are reported, but their roles do not establish autonomous local rule choice.
items.scope: Mapped field gradients, pulse histories, intervention logs, matched local states, and controls with and without targeted guidance.
items.next_discriminating_criticism_or_test: Hold the local pair and boundary fixed while randomizing remote field geometry and intervention; predictive dependence on those controls falsifies the claimed local sufficiency.
items.non_claims: This topic does not assume global drive is computationally free, uniform, nonselective in practice, or separable from the mechanism.

items.title: Ask whether recurring actuation belongs in a fifth search-space axis
items.open_problem: When a computation requires recurring drive or guided intervention, should that control resource be represented as a fifth categorical dimension rather than hidden inside mechanism or protocol?
items.why_open: The current governed registry has four axes; repeated actuation can vary independently and may change comparative conclusions.
items.scope: A compatibility-preserving ontology proposal distinguishing one-time preparation, global recurring drive, spatial selection, feedback, and measurement-conditioned control.
items.next_discriminating_criticism_or_test: Classify existing and proposed experiments twice—with control embedded and with an explicit fifth axis—and test whether the latter resolves otherwise conflated comparisons without fragmenting identity.
items.non_claims: This topic does not add a fifth axis, alter canonical coordinates, rank research programs, or admit the illustrative conjecture.
